blocks.text: Custom geometry buffers for bespoke meshes
positions: flat array of xyz triplets
indices: optional flat array of triangle indices; omit for raw triangle soup (every 3 positions is one triangle, in order)
normals: optional flat array of xyz triplets
uvs: optional flat array of uv pairs

BespokeGeometrySpec = { positions: number[] indices?: number[] normals?: number[] uvs?: number[] colors?: number[] // Per-vertex linear RGB (4 floats each: r,g,b,a). Enables vertex-colored bespoke meshes. emissive?: number[] // Per-vertex emissive RGB (3 floats each). metalness?: number[] // Per-vertex metalness (1 float each). roughness?: number[] // Per-vertex roughness (1 float each). textureRuns?: { texture: string; start: number; count: number }[] // Contiguous triangle-index ranges drawn with a texture (scripted geometry bakes these via ctx.albedo()). instances?: { // The INSTANCE SET: the mesh is drawn as many copies of one object, each copy its own typed record: a grass patch, a flock, a rubble field, a meadow in one draw. `layout` names the record's fields in WebGPU's vertex-format words (`{ offset: "float32x3", yaw: "unorm8", phase: "unorm8" }`, packed at natural alignment, stride rounded to 4 bytes); `data` is every record's components in layout order, flat. Reserved names the engine composes: `offset` (where the copy stands, metres in the object's frame), `yaw` (degrees about +Y; a unorm spans 0..360), `scale` (uniform or x3), `tint` (a colour multiplier); every other field is read in a material as `attribute("phase", "float")`. `lods` are index ranges in three.js LOD order (level 0 from 0 m, each later level from its `distance`), picked by the eye's distance: per copy where `offset` places it, and at full detail a level whose `distance` passes the radius of the whole set's room waits for the room's own distance (a tile's far cards switch with the tile); `bounds` the whole set's room (a swaying set declares it, and is culled); `count` the drawn prefix (default every record), drawn whole on every device: a record is a placement, never thinned. A geometry script declares the same set with `ctx.instances(...)` + `ctx.instance(...)`. `data[i] = v` moves one number. With no `layout` and no `data` the set stores no record: `count` copies, as many as one draw holds, each placed by the material from its copy number (`instanceIndex`), and `bounds` the room it moves them in. A copy a pixel or two wide is a point, not a mesh: a crowd of dots is a `points` row (`spawn api PointsPrimitiveSpec`). layout?: Record<string, string> data?: number[] count?: number lods?: { indices: [number, number]; distance?: number }[] bounds?: { min: [number, number, number]; max: [number, number, number] } } bounds?: { min: [number, number, number]; max: [number, number, number] } // `bounds` (min/max, metres in the object's frame) is the room the drawn vertices stand in when a material moves them past the triangles, returned by `geometry(ctx)` beside `uvs`; the cull and `.bounds` read it, the collider does not. revision?: number }

code.text:
BespokeGeometrySpec = {
  positions: number[]
  indices?: number[]
  normals?: number[]
  uvs?: number[]
  colors?: number[]   // Per-vertex linear RGB (4 floats each: r,g,b,a). Enables vertex-colored bespoke meshes.
  emissive?: number[]   // Per-vertex emissive RGB (3 floats each).
  metalness?: number[]   // Per-vertex metalness (1 float each).
  roughness?: number[]   // Per-vertex roughness (1 float each).
  textureRuns?: { texture: string; start: number; count: number }[]   // Contiguous triangle-index ranges drawn with a texture (scripted geometry bakes these via ctx.albedo()).
  instances?: {   // The INSTANCE SET: the mesh is drawn as many copies of one object, each copy its own typed record: a grass patch, a flock, a rubble field, a meadow in one draw. `layout` names the record's fields in WebGPU's vertex-format words (`{ offset: "float32x3", yaw: "unorm8", phase: "unorm8" }`, packed at natural alignment, stride rounded to 4 bytes); `data` is every record's components in layout order, flat. Reserved names the engine composes: `offset` (where the copy stands, metres in the object's frame), `yaw` (degrees about +Y; a unorm spans 0..360), `scale` (uniform or x3), `tint` (a colour multiplier); every other field is read in a material as `attribute("phase", "float")`. `lods` are index ranges in three.js LOD order (level 0 from 0 m, each later level from its `distance`), picked by the eye's distance: per copy where `offset` places it, and at full detail a level whose `distance` passes the radius of the whole set's room waits for the room's own distance (a tile's far cards switch with the tile); `bounds` the whole set's room (a swaying set declares it, and is culled); `count` the drawn prefix (default every record), drawn whole on every device: a record is a placement, never thinned. A geometry script declares the same set with `ctx.instances(...)` + `ctx.instance(...)`. `data[i] = v` moves one number. With no `layout` and no `data` the set stores no record: `count` copies, as many as one draw holds, each placed by the material from its copy number (`instanceIndex`), and `bounds` the room it moves them in. A copy a pixel or two wide is a point, not a mesh: a crowd of dots is a `points` row (`spawn api PointsPrimitiveSpec`).
    layout?: Record<string, string>
    data?: number[]
    count?: number
    lods?: { indices: [number, number]; distance?: number }[]
    bounds?: { min: [number, number, number]; max: [number, number, number] }
  }
  bounds?: { min: [number, number, number]; max: [number, number, number] }   // `bounds` (min/max, metres in the object's frame) is the room the drawn vertices stand in when a material moves them past the triangles, returned by `geometry(ctx)` beside `uvs`; the cull and `.bounds` read it, the collider does not.
  revision?: number
}
